title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
summary: The analyzer crashed when a type had repeated keys, or mixed integer and string keys. The AI changed TypeCollector.cs so the analyzer reports MsgPack005 instead. It keeps the first member for each key, and skips a member with the wrong key kind once it is reported. It also added analyzer tests, execution tests and a README section on opting out of source generation.
head: 9007cee1

claims.claim: The analyzer no longer crashes on duplicate integer keys, duplicate string keys or mixed key kinds. It reports MsgPack005 instead, with or without SuppressSourceGeneration.
claims.why_this_tier: 4 new tests fail before the change, because the analyzer crashes (AD0001) next to the MsgPack005. They pass after.

claims.claim: After the change, the real TypeCollector never throws on any list of 1 to 4 keyed members with integer or string keys. Before the change, it threw on most of them.
claims.why_this_tier: A formal model, written in Dafny, proves this for lists of any length. The model matches the real C# code on every input up to 4 members. The weakest step is a test: the real code throws before the change and not after.

chain.link: The Dafny model proves BranchNeverFailsForIntAndStringKeys with no unproven assumptions.
The model matches the real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs, before and after the change, with 0 mismatches.

claims.claim: The fix is incomplete. If a type's first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)], the analyzer still crashes (AD0001, ArgumentNullException). This also happens with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
claims.why_this_tier: An experiment on the real analyzer shows the crash before and after the change. That shows a gap in the fix, not a passing check, so it needs the owner to decide.

claims.claim: The change hides a diagnostic. The new `continue` also skips collecting the member's type. So a member with a mixed key and an unserializable type no longer gets MsgPack003. Before the change, it got MsgPack003 when the first key was a string.
claims.why_this_tier: It drops a diagnostic the old code reported. Whether that is fine, given the same member already gets the MsgPack005 error, is a product decision that needs the owner to decide.

claims.claim: Every repeated key is reported. When two members share a key, the first one is kept and the second gets MsgPack005 ('must be unique').
claims.why_this_tier: The duplicate-key tests fail before the change and pass after. The model's proof DupReported matches the real C# code on every input up to 4 members.

chain.link: The Dafny model proves DupReported: the first member wins and every repeat is reported.
The model matches the real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs.
The duplicate-key tests fail before the change and pass after.

claims.claim: The fix is copied into both the properties loop and the fields loop, which adds duplicate code to TypeCollector.cs.
claims.why_this_tier: The numbers come from a script that measures duplicate code and complexity, run before and after the change.

claims.claim: 4 of the 8 new analyzer tests already pass before the change, so they guard old behaviour and do not show the fix works. They cover a missing key, AllowPrivate, the member type and generation-only diagnostics.
claims.why_this_tier: The count comes from running the tests before and after the change.

claims.claim: A type with SuppressSourceGeneration gets no generated formatter, and still round-trips through the run-time (dynamic) resolver. The 2 new execution tests are meant to show this.
claims.why_this_tier: Both tests build and pass with SDK 9.0.321, but they also pass on the old code, so they guard the behaviour rather than prove the fix.

claims.claim: The new README section says the analyzer still checks suppressed types for MsgPack003, 004, 005, 012 and 015, and skips MsgPack011, 016 and 017 for them.
claims.why_this_tier: It is documentation. Tests cover 003, 004, 005, 015 and the skipped ones, but not 012. And C-2234-03 shows a case where the MsgPack005 check still crashes.

found: The change loses a diagnostic. The new `continue` skips CollectCore for the member's type, so a member with a mixed key no longer gets MsgPack003 (C-2234-04). We found this with an experiment on the real analyzer.

The fix is incomplete. If the first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)], the analyzer still crashes with ArgumentNullException, before and after the change, with SuppressSourceGeneration too (C-2234-03). The cause: the properties loop checks `else if (stringKey is not null)`, but the fields loop uses a bare `else`. We found this with an experiment on the real analyzer and with the Dafny model.

The goal in our task notes is false for the real code: 'collecting keys never fails, whatever keys repeat or mix kinds'. Dafny proves the exact condition instead: it fails exactly when the first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)].
One suspected problem turned out fine: with a repeated key, the first member is kept and the second gets MsgPack005 (C-2234-05).

The crash on repeated keys is not specific to suppressed types. It also happens without SuppressSourceGeneration: the test DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes fails before the change. And 4 of the 8 analyzer tests show the analyzer already checked suppressed types before the change.
SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs breaks style rule SA1649: the file name does not match the name of its first type.
An older bug, outside the diff: the fields loop reports BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull without message arguments, so the message reads 'Both int and string keys are null: {0}.{1}'.

refused.what: C-2234-04: the `continue` drops MsgPack003 for members with a mixed key.
refused.why: Dropping a diagnostic the old code reported is a product decision, so it needs the analyzer owner to decide.

scope_drift: The README gains a 14-line section, 'Opting out of source generation'. The issue title asks for an analyzer fix, not documentation.
not_checked: The code the source generator emits for repeated or mixed keys, when the first member wins. The generator shows no diagnostics here (reportDiagnostic is null).
Whether suppressed types get MsgPack012 (inaccessible types), as the README claims.
The full test suite after the change. We ran only the new tests and our experiments.
Members with no [Key] attribute, inherited members, and records with positional parameters. The model does not cover them.
The model only tries keys 0, 1, "a", "b" and null, with up to 4 members. So the model-versus-C# check covers 3710 inputs, not all inputs.
The issue body: we had only the issue title.
